card.does: Mild hydride. Aldehyde → 1° alcohol, ketone → 2° alcohol.
card.doesNot: Leaves C=C, esters and carboxylic acids alone.

label: LiAlH₄
name: Lithium aluminium hydride (in dry ether or THF)

card.does: Strong hydride. Aldehydes, ketones, acids and esters → alcohols (an ester gives two).
card.doesNot: Needs a separate H₂O workup step. Does not touch isolated C=C.

card.does: Reduces C=C to C–C and aldehyde/ketone C=O to the alcohol.
card.doesNot: Not used for esters, acids or benzene rings in this course.

card.does: Step 1 of hydroboration: B and H add syn across the C=C, B on the less substituted carbon.
card.doesNot: Gives no alcohol by itself; needs H₂O₂/NaOH.

card.does: Step 2 of hydroboration: swaps the C–B bond for C–OH with retention.
card.doesNot: Does nothing to an alkene on its own.

label: OsO₄
name: Osmium tetroxide, then NaHSO₃/H₂O (or cat. OsO₄ + NMO)

card.does: Syn dihydroxylation: two OH groups on the same face of the C=C. C–C bond kept.
card.doesNot: Does not cleave the C=C (that is O₃).

card.does: 1° alcohol → carboxylic acid; 2° alcohol → ketone.
card.doesNot: 3° alcohols: no reaction. Never stops at the aldehyde.

card.does: 1° alcohol → aldehyde (stops there); 2° alcohol → ketone.
card.doesNot: Leaves C=C alone; does not cleave C–C bonds; no acids.

card.does: Cleaves the C–C bond of a vicinal diol; each carbon becomes an aldehyde or ketone.
card.doesNot: Does nothing to an isolated alcohol or a 1,3-diol.

card.does: ROH → RCl.
card.doesNot: Not an oxidant or a reductant.

card.does: 1°/2° ROH → RBr by SN2, no rearrangement.
card.doesNot: Not for 3° alcohols; not an oxidant.

card.does: ROH → RBr (3° fast, SN1; 1° by SN2).
card.trap: Light does nothing useful here; keep the lamp off.

card.does: Dehydrates alcohols to the Zaitsev alkene (E1); 1° alcohols at 180 °C, ether at 140 °C.
card.doesNot: Not an oxidant.

label: NaNO₂ / H₂SO₄
name: Sodium nitrite in sulfuric (or hydrochloric) acid

card.does: Makes HONO; at 0–5 °C converts Ar–NH₂ into the aryl diazonium salt Ar–N₂⁺.
card.doesNot: Not a nitrating agent: it never puts NO₂ on a ring.

card.does: Electrophilic nitration: adds NO₂ to a ring C–H (o/p to OH, NH₂, OR).
card.trap: Looks like NaNO₂ on a tired day. It is not the diazonium route.

card.does: Strong base: deprotonates phenols (pKa ≈ 10) and carboxylic acids.
card.doesNot: Too weak to deprotonate an ordinary alcohol completely; does not replace NH₂ or OH on a ring.

card.does: Quenches hydride/Grignard alkoxides to the alcohol (room temp). With heat, converts Ar–N₂⁺ into Ar–OH.
card.doesNot: Does nothing useful before the hydride or Grignard has reacted.

card.does: Acidic workup: protonates alkoxides and carboxylates. As a reagent on an alkene it gives Markovnikov hydration.
card.doesNot: Kills a Grignard or hydride if added too early.

card.does: Strong base: deprotonates an alcohol completely to the alkoxide (step 1 of a Williamson).
card.doesNot: Not a nucleophile and not a reducing agent.

card.does: Deprotonates an alcohol to the alkoxide (with H₂ gas), like NaH.
card.doesNot: Not a nucleophile.

card.does: Perfect SN2 electrophile: methylates alkoxides, phenoxides, thiolates and sulfides.
card.doesNot: Cannot be eliminated (no β-hydrogens).

card.does: 1° halide: SN2 electrophile for alkoxides (Williamson).
card.doesNot: Elimination is minor with a 1° halide.

card.does: Benzylic 1° halide: excellent SN2 electrophile (Williamson).
card.doesNot: No β-hydrogens on the benzylic carbon's neighbour, so no E2.

card.does: Allylic 1° halide: excellent SN2 electrophile (Williamson).
card.doesNot: Does not add across its own C=C under these conditions.

card.does: 3° halide: E2 with alkoxides, SN1/E1 with weak nucleophiles.
card.trap: Never the electrophile in a Williamson ether synthesis.

card.does: 2° halide: mostly E2 with alkoxides.
card.trap: Put the isopropyl group on the alkoxide side instead.

card.does: Lewis acid catalyst for Friedel–Crafts C-acylation and the Fries rearrangement.
card.trap: Not a base. It cannot make an alkoxide for a Williamson synthesis.

card.does: Alkene → epoxide (syn, stereospecific).
card.trap: Not a diol reagent: OsO₄ gives the syn diol.

card.does: Cleaves C=C into two carbonyls.
card.trap: Decoy for OsO₄: OsO₄ keeps the C–C bond and gives a syn diol.

card.does: Strong, unselective oxidant that cleaves C=C bonds.
card.trap: Not in the toolkit as a selective reagent: use OsO₄ for diols, Jones or PCC for alcohols.
